podcast.body: This album is widely considered an "absolute disaster" and the "worst album in Swans' entire career." It was the result of the band's unexpected popularity from their "Love Will Tear Us Apart" cover, which led them to sign with a major label and work with significant economic resources and a professional producer for the first time. The album sweetened and relaxed Swans' sound, introducing much more banal lyrics, including classic love songs that were completely out of character for the band. It featured much more melodic music with influences from country, Americana, and folk, which clashed with Swans' established discourse. The album failed to convince anyone: classic fans were horrified (even by the cover art), and the new audience gained from the single was neither loyal nor knew what to expect. Critically panned, disliked by the band, and a commercial failure, it is seen as the beginning of the end for the first iteration of Swans, which dissolved in the mid-90s. "El resultado, pues, Borning Wall de 1989, un absoluto desastre, el peor desastre y el peor disco de toda la carrera de suans."
